headline: Doubling your HGH dose
punch: There is a randomised trial on this.

headline: Does height scale with dose?
body: So the standard advice you will read everywhere is to take as much as you can afford. Sitting underneath that advice is an assumption nobody states out loud, which is that height gain scales with dose in something like a straight line. Double the input, double the output. | That assumption has actually been tested properly, in a randomised trial, with children followed all the way to near-adult height. And the answer is a specific number rather than an opinion.
punch: Somebody ran the experiment. Here is what it gave.

headline: Mauras 2000
body: GH-deficient adolescents were randomly assigned to one of two doses and then followed to near-adult height, defined as a bone age of 16 or more in males and 14 or more in females. | Standard group: **0.3 mg per kg per week**. High dose group: **0.7 mg per kg per week**. That is more than double, same drug, same daily subcutaneous injections, same monitoring. The only variable that differed between those two groups was how much went in.
punch: _A real randomisation, not two clinics being compared._

headline: 4.6 centimetres
body: Subjects in the high dose group were significantly taller at near-adult height by an average of **4.6 cm**, P < 0.001, n = 75, with a 95% confidence interval of 2.6 to 6.5 cm. For those treated at least 4 years the gap widened to **5.7 cm**. | So more than double the dose, sustained for years, bought about four and a half centimetres. Ranke's 2021 review summarises the same trial the same way, at roughly 4 cm for a doubling.

headline: In growth rate terms
body: Before the study started both groups were growing at **8.5 cm per year**, which tells you the randomisation worked. In the first year on study the high dose group hit **9.8 cm per year** against **8.2** in the standard group, P = 0.001 between groups. | What this means is that the difference is genuine and statistically solid, and also much smaller than doubling the input would lead you to expect. The curve bends hard, early.

headline: What surprised me
body: Everyone assumes high dose GH burns through your growth plates faster, trading future height for present height. The trial measured it directly and that is not what happened. | Bone ages advanced **approximately 1 year per chronological year in both** the standard and the high dose groups. The paper states outright that high dose rhGH **did not increase the rate of skeletal maturation**. | So the thing everybody worries about did not occur at twice the standard clinical dose.
punch: _More GH did not age the plates faster._

headline: It was not free
body: The cost was real, it just appeared somewhere other than bone age. At any given point in time roughly **28%** of the high dose group had IGF-1 above the normal range, against about **9%** in the standard group. | And the high dose group showed a greater increase in fasting insulin, P = 0.011, and C-peptide, P = 0.019. Glucose handling moved measurably. So the trade was not height against bone age. It was height against metabolic markers.
punch: The cost showed up in insulin, not in bone age.

headline: Who this applies to
body: Every single number in this post comes from adolescents with diagnosed **GH deficiency** receiving replacement therapy. These were children with a broken axis and the drug was fixing it. | What a doubling does on top of a normal, intact GH axis was not tested here and this trial cannot answer it. Anyone quoting 4.6 cm as what doubling your dose will do for you is extending a replacement result into an enhancement claim.
punch: ==This is replacement data, not enhancement data.==

headline: So what does this buy you?
body: Treat the dose response as a curve that bends rather than a line that climbs. The trial that more than doubled the dose bought 4.6 cm over years, and an independent review summarises it the same way. | The thing that did not go wrong was skeletal maturation. The thing that did move was insulin and IGF-1 overshoot. And all of it is in people whose axis was deficient to begin with.
punch: Doubling the dose buys centimetres, not inches.
